newsitem.title: TURKEY: OLYMPICS-ISTANBUL SLAMS REPORT ON ITS OLYMPIC BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-ISTANBUL SLAMS REPORT ON ITS OLYMPIC BID.

text.p: The head of Istanbul's bid to host the Olympic games in 2004 slammed the evaluation report on the city's bid by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) released last week.

"The IOC report does not reflect Istanbul as the winning candidate that it really is...There are factual mistakes in the charts given, and both discrepancies and omissions in the written text," Yalcin Aksoy, general director of the Istanbul Olympic Bidding Committee told Reuters on Tuesday.

The report cast doubts on Istanbul's transport facilities, the siting of athletes, judges and media in a single Olympic village and calls for clarification of the country's Olympic law which underpins the city's bid.
The IOC will announce on March 7 a shortlist of five cities from the original 11 contenders. The final choice will be made on September 5.
Rome and Athens have emerged as the early favourites to get the Games but Aksoy said he was confident that Istanbul would make it through to the final five.
"I'm sure that we have secured our place amongst the finalists," he said.
